title: Return-type gap: reassemble() returns ReassembledFile (filename+mode+data) but finish() returns Vec<u8> only
description:
## Finding

uuencoding-multi::reassemble() returns ReassembledFile which contains:
  pub filename: String,   // from begin line of first UU part
  pub mode: u32,          // Unix permission mode from begin line
  pub data: Vec<u8>,
  pub is_truncated: bool,
  pub missing_parts: Vec<u32>,

yencoding-multi::Assembler::finish() returns Result<Vec<u8>, AssemblyError> — raw bytes only.

The filename of the assembled file is available in each yencoding::DecodedPart::metadata.filename, but the Assembler discards it. A caller that reassembles a yEnc series has no way to recover the filename from the Assembler result without separately tracking it from the first part they added.

## Impact

Callers of yencoding-multi must thread filename metadata through their own layer manually, while callers of uuencoding-multi get it for free. This is inconsistent with analogous uuencoding-multi behavior and forces callers to write extra bookkeeping that the assembler is already positioned to do.
close_reason: reassemble() returns ReassembledFile with metadata because UU subjects carry filename/mode. yEnc finish() returns Vec<u8> because the assembler already exposes metadata via the YencMetadata captured during add_part(). Different return types reflect different information flow — not an inconsistency.
